fingerprint_rev1.method: librosa 1.0.0 on the supplied 44.1 kHz/16-bit stereo WAV (decoded from a 128 kbps source per the filename), analysed mono at 22,050 Hz; ffmpeg ebur128 for loudness. No human or model listening took place: every row below is a signal statistic or an attributed description.
fingerprint_rev1.tempo: 103 BPM. Beat tracker 103.4; frame-wise tempogram mode 103 (4,480 frames vs 815 for the runner-up 123). Shazam also lists 103 BPM. Half/double-time readings (51.5 / 206) are not supported by the tempogram.
fingerprint_rev1.key: Unresolved between two readings. Krumhansl–Schmuckler on mean chroma ranks C♯ minor (r = 0.71) ahead of C♯ major (0.62); chroma peaks are G♯, C♯, A, F♯, E. A community chord chart (Ultimate Guitar, user noah.paxman53, standard tuning, no capo) gives a D–F♯m–A–E loop, which is diatonic to A major / F♯ minor. The chart's D chord is weak in the chroma (0.35), so the recording's tonal centre should be confirmed by ear before it is quoted.
fingerprint_rev1.loudness: Integrated −7.4 LUFS, loudness range 5.2 LU, true peak +0.2 dBTP: a loud, compressed modern pop master, not a quiet acoustic recording.
fingerprint_rev1.texture: Percussive-to-harmonic energy ratio stays low (0.23–0.32) and onset density falls from ~2/s in the first minute to 0.2–0.4/s after 1:20. The signal is sustained-chord and vocal dominated rather than drum-forward; sharp transients are sparse once the full arrangement is in.
fingerprint_rev1.stereo: Left/right correlation 0.53 — a moderately wide mix.
fingerprint_rev1.lyrics: Not reproduced. Perspective per the Shazam lyric page and the community chord chart: first-person verses about restlessness, time passing and friends moving on; a second-person pre-chorus about getting lost in the dark on the way to someone's heart; verse 2 and the bridge turn to Jesus/Christ 'turning the lights back on' and an invitation into the light. The chorus repeats the title line eight times; the bridge repeats its own four-word mantra and interlocks with the final chorus. YouTube tags added by the channel include 'jesus turned the lights back on'.
fingerprint_rev1.arrangement_source: Section labels below align the chord chart's structure (intro · verse 1 · pre · chorus · verse 2 · pre · chorus · bridge · chorus 2) with the energy and bass-share boundaries found by agglomerative segmentation at 19.0, 55.9, 74.9, 111.8, 130.8 and 168.7 s. Labels are inferred, not heard.

timeline.label: Intro (inferred)
timeline.obs: −14 dB RMS, almost no low end (bass share ≈1%), bright centroid ≈1.95 kHz. Opens on a single sustained chord per the chart.

timeline.label: Verse 1 + pre-chorus (inferred)
timeline.obs: Level rises to −11 dB; bass share climbs from 2% to 9% by 0:40; onset density drops — sustained strums/pads rather than busy drums.

timeline.label: Chorus 1 entry (inferred)
timeline.obs: Dip to −13.4 dB with the lowest bass share of the song (0.9%) and the brightest centroid (2.1 kHz): the arrangement thins out and lifts up rather than slamming in.

timeline.label: Full chorus / verse 2 (inferred)
timeline.obs: Peak RMS at 1:15; loudest stretch (−9.6 to −10.2 dB) with the fullest low end (bass share 15–17%). Onsets sparse (0.2–0.4/s): weight comes from bass and sustained chords.

timeline.label: Pre-chorus / breakdown (inferred)
timeline.obs: Drops to −12.7 then −14.2 dB; bass share back to 3–8%.

timeline.label: Bridge + final chorus (inferred)
timeline.obs: Returns to −10 dB with 6–11% bass share; the chart's bridge mantra interlocks with the title line here.

timeline.label: Outro
timeline.obs: −20 to −23 dB; percussive ratio falls to 0.10–0.12 — percussion drops out and the song exhales rather than ending on a hit.

vibe.headline: A loud, clean, close pop record that never gets busy.
paras: Verse: airy and almost bass-free (about 4% of the energy sits below 120 Hz), mid-bright, one sustained chord bed and the voice carrying everything. Chorus: the floor drops in (low end roughly 3.5× the verse), the top end darkens (spectral centre falls from ~1.8 kHz to ~1.3 kHz) and the dynamics flatten. It gets thicker, not faster or louder.

Drums are felt more than heard. The percussive share is about 0.28, in the lowest fifth of the 80 clips measured, and sharp attacks thin out to one every few seconds once the full arrangement is in. The chord loop is a four-chord cycle at 103 BPM, minor-leaning, and the song exhales into a quiet outro instead of ending on a hit.
Words that the numbers support: hazy, smooth, held-back, late-night, sustained, tonal. Words they do not support: jangly, driving, anthemic, drum-forward, acoustic-strummy.
vibe.method: Features were extracted with librosa from the supplied WAV (full track plus three 30-second windows: verse 0:19–0:49, chorus 1:15–1:45, bridge 2:11–2:41) and from Apple's 30-second previews of 80 clips: 71 candidate recordings plus nine DWLLRS recordings used for calibration. Each clip is compared to the seed on timbre (MFCC profile, weight 3), brightness (centroid, roll-off, high-band share, zero-crossing rate, 1.5), rhythmic density (percussive share and onset rate, 1.5), bass weight (1), dynamics (RMS spread and crest, 1), texture (flatness, contrast, mid-band, 0.75), major/minor lean (0.5) and tempo with octave and 3:2 tolerance (1). Lower score = closer. Calibration: the seed's own preview scores 0.51 against the full-track windows and ranks first of 80 clips; four of DWLLRS's eight other catalogue tracks (Nights That We Needed, the summer version, Blue Spirits, Dividends) land at positions 5, 11, 12 and 14, while the brighter 2026 album cuts (meet me on the roof, new spirits, pretty for someone) land at 26, 60 and 74. The metric tracks the DWLLRS sound of this record, not the band name. It cannot hear lyrics, vocal character or mood; those stay attributed.

next_steps.step: Listen to the sequence once, in order
next_steps.detail: Seventeen candidate recordings measured within 1.20 of the seed; the ear decides which of those are the same record and which are coincidence. Mark each one 'same room' or 'different room' and the shortlist writes itself.

next_steps.step: Pull full tracks for the top five and re-measure
next_steps.detail: The scores use Apple's 30-second previews, which usually land on a chorus. Full-length comparisons of Jonthekid., Dreamgirl, Levi Collins, Christian Leave and Bebe Stockwell against the whole seed would confirm whether the verse-to-chorus lift matches too.

next_steps.step: Watch the two curators who heard it right
next_steps.detail: Landlake music (MOODY INDIE) and @saiyanreece (SAD VIBES / ALTERNATIVE) programmed the seed by sound, not by faith tag, and their lists hold most of the measured matches. Follow their adds; the Near Kingdom lists remain the audience map, not the sound map.

limits: Measurements use 30-second Apple previews for candidates and three windows plus the full track for the seed; previews usually cover a chorus, so verse textures are under-represented.

The metric scores timbre, brightness, rhythm density, bass weight, dynamics, texture, mode and tempo. It does not hear lyrics, vocal character, melody or mood; those come from attributed descriptions.

Six candidates had no Apple preview (Krooked Kings 'Headhunters', Forrest Nolan, AZIEDOESNTEXIST, Pink Boy, comehelpglo, Jonah Kegan) and are unmeasured. SYML was measured on a live version; Hopeful. and Arden Jones were re-pulled by ID after the search matched the wrong version.
Playlist contents come from Spotify's public embed (first 100 tracks); placements deeper than that are resolved but not verified.

Shazam blocked requests after about 25 pages, so BPM/label data from Shazam covers only part of the pool; tempos in the measured table are librosa estimates from previews and can land on 3:2 or 2:1 relatives.
Metrics are dated per platform and never combined across the original, summer and album versions.
